title: 2024年12月四级真题 第1套 阅读2
paperTitle: 2024年12月大学英语四级真题（第1套）
passage:
P1 Engineering in the U.S. has long been a male-dominated profession. Fifty years ago, it looked like that might change.

P2 In 1970, the percentage of women majoring in engineering was less than 1%. In 1979, that number was 9%. Many hoped women would continue to enter the field at the same rate. But that's not what happened. Today, only 21% of engineering majors are women, a number largely unchanged since 2000.

P3 I am a historian who, along with my colleagues, surveyed 251 women engineers who graduated from college in the 1970s. These pioneers reflected on the challenges they faced—and had advice for women entering the field today.

P4 One survey taker explained, "The greatest challenge for me was continuing to believe in myself, when all the messages I was getting were that I would never be taken seriously or promoted or given raises at the same rate as men, who were clearly less qualified and not as smart as I was."

P5 A chemical engineer who worked in manufacturing agreed, "You have to prove yourself just because you are female. And you have to work twice as hard!"

P6 A civil engineer said, "We are 'women engineers.' People don't refer to a man as a 'man engineer'—he's an engineer. We are constantly reminded that we don't truly belong." Another civil engineer stated, "On many levels, you're never quite one of the groups."

P7 Women also talked about family caregiving responsibilities. A retired vice president from a major chemical company stated, "Young women engineers are on an equal footing until they have children, then they struggle to balance work and family—and compete with men who don't have the same household responsibilities."

P8 But over the years things have changed a lot. Young women engineers are more accepted mostly because there are just more of them.

P9 Many women engineers hailed the benefits of their chosen career. A program manager in manufacturing stated that engineering is the best degree. A mechanical engineer said, "It will give you the flexibility to do almost anything. It is also satisfying to see the effects of what you have done."

questions.q: What does the passage say about the engineering profession in the United States?
options: It has seen a change in attitude towards women engineers since 1979.
It witnessed a significant increase in women engineers in the 1970s.
It has experienced the gradual weakening of male dominance.
It boasted the largest number of engineering majors in 2000.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the passage say about the engineering profession in the United States 没 有 infer/imply/mainly about 等推断或主旨标志，问 "the passage say"，是对原文已陈述 事实的核对，属四级最高频的细节题。

【拆句】题干主干是 What does the passage say about ...，是 say about 后接宾语的特殊疑问 句，结构平铺直叙、无陷阱，只要知道 say about="就……说了什么"即可。

【定位】In 1970, the percentage of women majoring in engineering was less than 1%. In 1979, that number was 9%. Many hoped women would continue to enter the field at the same rate. But that's not what happened. 1970 年，主修工程的女性占比不到 1%；1979 年这一数字升至 9%。许多人本希望女性能 以同样速度持续进入这一行业，但事实并非如此。

【选项】A) 无中生有 原文只给比例数据，没有提任何"对待女工程师态度的变化"，a change in attitude towards women engineers since 1979 属于凭空添加新概念。 B) ✓ 正确 In 1970, the percentage of women majoring in engineering was less than 1%. In 1979, that number was 9% ↔It witnessed a significant increase in women engineers in the 1970s In 1970 和 In 1979 ↔in the 1970s 预判要的是"70 年代女工程师比例大幅上升"，B 项 significant increase in women engineers in the 1970s 几乎逐词对应，无需犹豫即可锁定。 C) 与原文相反 Today, only 21% of engineering majors are women, a number largely unchanged since 2000 明确说自 2000 年起男性主导未弱化，与 gradual weakening of male dominance 直接相反。 D) 偷换概念 原文 2000 年只是"21% 未变"的起算点，并未说 2000 年工程专业人数达到最大， boasted the largest number of engineering majors in 2000 属于把时间词原样搬， 结论却换了内容。 一位受访者表示她面临的最大挑战是什么? A) 不对资质较低的男性工程师产生优越感。 B) 不把她收到的所有信息都当真。 C) 在升职或加薪时不过高评价自己的资历。 D) 尽管不断受到打击或遭受不公平待遇,仍不失去自信。

questions.q: What does one survey taker say was her greatest challenge?
options: Not to feel superior to less qualified male engineers.
Not to take seriously all the messages she was getting.
Not to think highly of her qualifications when promoted or given a pay raise.
Not to lose self-confidence though constantly discouraged or unfairly treated.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does one survey taker say was her greatest challenge 是对原文一句引语的客观 还原，属细节题。

【拆句】What does one survey taker say was her greatest challenge 是个嵌套问句，say 后面 接的是 "(that) her greatest challenge was ____"，疑问词 What 提到了句首，回原文找 "挑战是 ____" 这层语义即可。

【定位】The greatest challenge for me was continuing to believe in myself, when all the messages I was getting were that I would never be taken seriously or promoted or given raises at the same rate as men, who were clearly less qualified and not as smart as I was. 我最大的挑战是在收到"我永远不会像男性那样被认真对待、被晋升或被加薪——而那些男 性明显不如我合格、不如我聪明"这类信息时，仍然继续相信自己。

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文受访者只是说"那些男性明显不如我合格"，是事实陈述；Not to feel superior to less qualified male engineers 把它扭曲成"不要觉得自己高人一等"，方向截然不同。 B) 答非所问 原文 all the messages I was getting 是"挑战的背景"，不是"挑战本身"；B 项却把"不 要把这些信息当真"说成挑战，错把背景当主体。 C) 与原文相反 原文说"她被晋升/加薪的待遇不如男性"，C 项却说"在被晋升/加薪时不要看高自己的资 历"，既颠倒了情境（她没有被同等晋升），也错读了态度。 D) ✓ 正确 continuing to believe in myself ↔Not to lose self-confidence all the messages I was getting were that I would never be taken seriously or promoted or given raises at the same rate as men ↔though constantly discouraged or unfairly treated 预判要"在打压中坚持自信"，D 项 Not to lose self-confidence though constantly discouraged or unfairly treated 两个要素全有，是定位句的精准同义替换。 根据两位土木工程师的说法,女性工程师经常有何感受? A) 在许多层面上不具备资格。 B) 被排除在团体之外。 C) 被所在组织过度使用。 D) 被男性同事看不起。

questions.q: How do women engineers frequently feel according to the two civil engineers?
options: Disqualified on many levels.
Excluded from the group.
Overworked by their organizations.
Looked down upon by male colleagues.
questions.explain:
【判型】How do women engineers frequently feel according to the two civil engineers 问的 是"她们感觉如何"，依据 according to 直接锁定原文两位 civil engineer 的话，是细节归 纳题。

【拆句】How do women engineers frequently feel according to the two civil engineers 主干 是 How do women engineers feel，frequently 是状语，according to ... 是介词短语作 状语，限定信息来源，没有从句也无否定，是直白的特殊疑问句。

【定位】A civil engineer said, "We are 'women engineers.' People don't refer to a man as a 'man engineer'—he's an engineer. We are constantly reminded that we don't truly belong." Another civil engineer stated, "On many levels, you're never quite one of the groups." 一位土木工程师说："我们被叫作'女工程师'。人们不会把男人叫'男工程师'——他就是工程 师。我们时刻被提醒：我们并不真正属于这里。"另一位土木工程师说："在很多层面上，你 从来不算这个圈子的一员。"

【选项】A) 偷换概念 原文 On many levels, you're never quite one of the groups 中的 on many levels 修 饰"在多个层面上"不属于群体，A 项 Disqualified on many levels 把它说成"在多个层 面上不合格"，是把"不属于群体"换成"不合格"。 B) ✓ 正确 We are constantly reminded that we don't truly belong ↔Excluded from the group you're never quite one of the groups ↔Excluded from the group 预判要"不属于/被排除的情绪"，B 项 Excluded from the group 直接对应两位受访者的 核心情感，是最稳的同义替换。 C) 张冠李戴 P6 全段谈的是"不属于群体"的归属感问题，根本未涉及工作量；Overworked by their organizations 是从 work twice as hard 借来的概念，硬塞进了 53 题。 D) 过度推断 原文两位土木工程师讲的是"被整个圈子提醒不属于"，并未具体说"是男同事看低自己"； Looked down upon by male colleagues 把抽象的群体压缩成"男同事"这一具体施 动者。 什么可能使年轻女性工程师在当今更容易被接受? A) 她们在获得平等地位方面取得的成功。 B) 她们平衡工作与家庭的能力。 C) 她们职责的改变。 D) 她们数量的增加。

questions.q: What probably makes young women engineers more accepted nowadays?
options: Their success in gaining an equal footing.
Their ability to balance work and family.
The change in their responsibilities.
The increase in their number.
questions.explain:
【判型】What probably makes young women engineers more accepted nowadays 看似含 probably 像推断，实质问"原文里给出的原因是什么"，原文已经直说理由，仍是细节题。

【拆句】What probably makes young women engineers more accepted nowadays 是 What makes sb. + 形容词 的使役结构，What 作主语，makes 是谓语，young women engineers 是宾语，more accepted nowadays 是宾语补足语，意为"是什么让年轻女工程 师如今更被接受"。

【定位】Young women engineers are more accepted mostly because there are just more of them. 年轻女工程师之所以如今更被接受，主要是因为她们的人数变多了。

【选项】A) 张冠李戴 原文 Young women engineers are on an equal footing until they have children 只 说"育前与男性平起平坐"，是过去就存在的状态，不是"如今更被接受"的新原因；A 项 Their success in gaining an equal footing 把它包装成新成就，归错原因。 B) 与原文相反 原文 then they struggle to balance work and family 明明说"在生育后她们挣扎于平 衡工作与家庭"，B 项却说"她们有能力平衡工作与家庭"，方向完全相反。 C) 无中生有 原文 compete with men who don't have the same household responsibilities 提 到"家庭责任不对等"，但从未说女工程师的责任发生了变化；C 项 The change in their responsibilities 是凭空增添一个变化。 D) ✓ 正确 there are just more of them ↔The increase in their number 预判要"人数变多"，D 项 The increase in their number 是这层意思的最贴近名词化表 达，无可争议。 从一位机械工程师的陈述中,我们可以对许多女性工程师得出什么结论? A) 她们对所选择的职业深感自豪。 B) 她们获得了灵活工作的好处。 C) 她们享受将工程工作做到最佳程度。 D) 她们已证明能够做几乎任何事情。

questions.q: What can we conclude about many female engineers from the statement of a mechanical engineer?
options: They take great pride in their chosen career.
They have reaped the benefits of being flexible.
They enjoy doing engineering to the best degree.
They have proved capable of doing almost anything.
questions.explain:
【判型】What can we conclude about many female engineers from the statement of a mechanical engineer 中的 conclude+from 是典型推断题信号，需要从一位受访者的具体 话语得出"许多女工程师"层面的结论。 55. What can we conclude about many female engineers from the statement of a mechanical engineer? A) They take great pride in their chosen career. B) They have reaped the benefits of being flexible. C) They enjoy doing engineering to the best degree. D) They have proved capable of doing almost anything.

【拆句】What can we conclude about many female engineers from the statement of a mechanical engineer 主干为 What can we conclude，about many female engineers 是 conclude 的对象，from the statement of a mechanical engineer 是信息来源；问的 是"从这位机械工程师的话里能得出关于许多女工程师的什么结论"。

【定位】Many women engineers hailed the benefits of their chosen career. A program manager in manufacturing stated that engineering is the best degree. A mechanical engineer said, "It will give you the flexibility to do almost anything. It is also satisfying to see the effects of what you have done." 许多女工程师都盛赞自己所选职业的好处。一位制造业项目经理说工程是最好的学位。一 位机械工程师说："它会给你几乎可以做任何事的灵活度，看到自己所做工作的成果也令人 满足。"

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 Many women engineers hailed the benefits of their chosen career ↔ They take great pride in their chosen career It is also satisfying to see the effects of what you have done ↔ take great pride in their chosen career 预判要"对职业感到自豪"，A 项 take great pride in their chosen career 在态度极性和 概括层级上都对得最准，是最贴预判的一项。 B) 偷换概念 原文 give you the flexibility to do almost anything 是说"这份职业能给你灵活度"， 强调的是职业本身的属性；B 项 reaped the benefits of being flexible 把它说成"她们 因"自己"灵活而获益"，把工具属性挪到了人本身。 C) 无中生有 原文 engineering is the best degree 是"工程是最好的学位"，整体作主系表；C 项 enjoy doing engineering to the best degree 把 the best degree 拆成 to the best degree（=最大程度地）作状语，意思变成"以最高程度享受做工程"，是字面拼凑出的 伪意思。 D) 过度推断 原文 give you the flexibility to do almost anything 是工程这个职业"能让你"做几乎 任何事，是潜在可能；D 项 proved capable of doing almost anything 说她们"已经 证明自己能做几乎任何事"，把可能性升级为既定事实。
